purpose: Forward-deployed engineer, AI deployment engineer, implementation-focused solutions engineer, and solutions architect roles: translate domain needs into working integrations, communicate technical tradeoffs, and carry systems through deployment and stabilization.
scopeDecisions: Lead with LLM integration and live production stabilization, then customer demonstrations and retailer-system integration. Preserve the primary grouped order and all eight source bullets.
Retain the original Head of Product description: CEO, executive-team, and investor communication supply relevant stakeholder scope.
Tailor RadiusAI toward technical demonstrations, capture hardware, training data, and POS integration. Keep the collaborative ‘helped develop’ qualification.
Use the internship timeline to show tools for domain experts; do not add its reserve bullet to the primary set.
Keep the clinician-facing platform explicitly a board-approved concept in its source bullet. Do not imply that this concept or the reserved cloud migration was shipped.
The headline is a target direction, not a claim of having held a forward-deployed engineer title or delivered external consulting engagements.
skillEvidence: Python/Django, cloud services, Cosmos DB, and deployment infrastructure are supported by the Pause architecture, classifier, takeover, and operations work.

REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Git, Linux, Azure OpenAI, stakeholder management, and PRDs are present in the master skills or competencies; the actual integration and demonstration work anchors this direction.
Docker is supported by the TA grading implementation. The PyTorch tool for plant engineers supports the domain-user enablement paragraph.
Do not add Kubernetes, Terraform, RAG, enterprise sales ownership, or a completed AWS-to-Azure migration without evidence.

contextReview.reason: Opening contribution says “the product” before this draft identifies what the product does. Briefly identify the women’s-health platform while keeping the LLM integration and architecture emphasis.
The preceding bullet introduces the companion; a pragmatic launch and retained backend directly support integration/deployment roles.
An inherited live production system could be the companion, backend, or entire platform. Name the platform scope rather than leaving the reader to infer the takeover’s boundaries.

The preceding Pause bullets establish the consumer app and companion. It clearly describes a board-approved concept, not a shipped clinician platform; useful requirements evidence with explicit limits.

First RadiusAI bullet says “system behavior” without naming the system demonstrated. Identify ShopAssist as a computer-vision assisted-checkout system. This also supplies context for the following integration and recognition bullets.
Explains the POS inputs, customer tracks, algorithm, and constraints. The flagged RAI-DS-09 introduction can establish the shared system; no separate rewrite is needed here.
Fits the integration and data-reconciliation narrative after the POS bullet. A system introduction in RAI-DS-09 resolves the group context.
The index and errors are introduced immediately before it. Supplies a quantified deployment-relevant result; keep the pair together.
